body:
Don't look now, but Texas looks like one of the most interesting teams in the country, meanwhile, the Longhorns' former Big 12 rival Nebraska is running out of earthly explanations for its struggles
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football's Week 10 was billed as a heavyweight battle and the results have already shown up. No. 3 Utah and No. 9 BYU played an instant class version of the Holy War rivalry and No. 23 Oregon stunned Ohio State at the Horseshoe. Seemingly every week, major playoff opportunities are on the line. No. 18 Missouri likely lost its shot, while No. 12 Ohio State and No. 14 LSU firmly moved to the outside of the bubble.  In the night slate, multiple top 10 teams put their seasons on the line. No. 1 Miami travels to face No. 11 Notre Dame in a must-win game for the Irish. No. 6 Kentucky also plays No. 13 Tennessee in a prove-it spot. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 10 heading into the primetime games. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: UtahWhen Utah joined the Big 12, they arrived with expectations of competing for the conference and nationally every year under Kyle Whittingham. It never happened. Finally, Morgan Scalley has them playing up to their potential and beating their rival. 
The No. 3 Utes pulled off a massive victory against No. 9 BYU, snapping a three-game losing streak against the Cougars. They overcame an early second-half deficit behind a tremendous game from quarterback Devon Dampier, rising to 9-0 for the first time since 2008 (an undefeated season). The win sharpies them into the College Football Playoff. Based on what happens tonight, they could have a serious case for No. 1. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Ohio StateThe last time Ohio State had three losses in the regular season was 2011, an interim-coached season after Tattoogate. The last time they gave up 38 unanswered points was in 1999, the penultimate year of the John Cooper era. In every way, Ryan Day's program is bottoming out. 
Granted, the quarterback injury to Julian Sayin stands tall during the Buckeyes' skid. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey has struggled in two starts, never quite getting on the same page with his downfield passing. But while Sayin and Jeremiah Smith managed to cover up many holes, they were wallpaper for rot growing in the walls. The Buckeyes were bullied on both lines of scrimmage against USC and Oregon, two teams that have been pushed around by much of the Big Ten. Their secondary collapsed. Ohio State is just not Ohio State right now in any phase, and Day better have good answers to fix it in 2027. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: LSULane Kiffin signed the biggest contract in the SEC and reportedly spent the most money on his roster in college football this year. After a 31-14 loss against No. 5 Alabama, all LSU has to show for it is an 0-3 record against CFP Top 25 opponents. 
LSU got completely outclassed against the Tide, who came up big in essentially every big moment. Kiffin's offense turned the ball over on downs three times and had multiple red zone trips end empty. It was Kiffin's sixth straight loss against Alabama as a head coach, and the Tigers' postseason hopes are on life support. There aren't many worse returns on investment in 2026. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: TexasDon't look now, but the Longhorns are looking awfully interesting heading into the home stretch. None of their performances have been especially clean, but No. 7 Texas now has wins over No. 7 Ole Miss, No. 12 Ohio State, No. 13 Tennessee and No. 18 Missouri on their record. 
There were a few frustrating moments, but Arch Manning played an efficient game with 297 yards passing and three touchdowns without a turnover. If he can avoid mistakes, Texas looks in good shape to reach the postseason, especially as they rank first in line as a potential three-loss team. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: NebraskaThere has to be a curse at Nebraska. There's no other explanation. The Cornhuskers had a 5-0 record and looked in prime position to crash the postseason. Now, they've lost three straight and haven't even comfortably reached bowl eligibility after a frustrating 24-13 loss against Illinois on Friday night. Nebraska got 426 yards of offense, but managed to turn it into only 13 points after multiple missed field goals and turnovers on downs. They went 1-of-4 on fourth down. After the game, Nebraska fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen. Will it help? Only if it can lift the curse. 
Winner: Ferris StateToo many people know Ferris State as the school that produced Trinidad Chambliss. Everyone should also know them as the most dominant college football team in America. The Bulldogs just won their 40th straight game, tying a Division II record, after an 80-0 win over Wayne State. The winning streak dates back to Chambliss's first solo start in 2024, but Tony Annese has built a machine in Big Rapids. Annese has an absurd 153-21 record with four national championships in the last five years. He's as good as it gets. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: TulaneWhen Jon Sumrall left for Florida, Tulane decided to take the easy way out and promote internally. Will Hall, a former coach at Southern Miss, was elevated from passing game coordinator to head coach. That decision has become an absolute unmitigated disaster. Despite returning a talented roster, Tulane has completely fallen off a cliff. 
A loss to Tulsa emphasizes just how far this proud program has fallen. The Green Wave lost 60-10, an astonishing result for the reigning American Conference champions. They're now sitting at 4-5 with games still remaining against North Texas and South Florida. Tulane could realistically miss a bowl game in 2026. After the showing last week, Hall should be a one-and-done coach. Tulane can -- and must -- do better.

President Donald Trump sparked the discussion on Saturday by posting his offer to White on social media

        Will UFC CEO and president Dana White be the next White House press secretary? President Donald Trump offered White the role on Saturday via social media. While a move seems unlikely, White confirmed Saturday that he is set to travel to Washington, D.C. for a meeting with POTUS on Monday, but he offered no further details."I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote, further listing a variety of current and former UFC athletes he hoped would join White as assistants, "even though some are not from our Country."White, 57, first played into speculation about the job offer with an AI-generated meme he posted on his Instagram stories shortly after the offer. It included a caption, "On to the next chapter." In a press conference following Zuffa Boxing 12 in London on Saturday, White said he has a meeting scheduled with the President on Monday.
"I got a lot of jobs already," White joked. "... I'm sure we'll have something to talk about after [the meeting]."Trump had extended assistant roles to Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison White, who joined UFC in 2001 after his business partners with Zuffa purchased the promotion, is also the face of two other combat sports brands under the TKO Group Holdings banner, Zuffa Boxing and Power Slap. 
If appointed, White would replace Katie Zacharia, who was dismissed after serving five days as press secretary in October. Karoline Leavitt, who held the role before Zacharia, stepped down in August to focus on family. As a former fight promoter, casino magnate and long-time fan of combat sports, Trump helped make sports history in June when he hosted the UFC Freedom 250 event on the south lawn of the White House. Trump hosted White's debut event as UFC president at his Trump Taj Mahal casino in 2001, and the two formed a friendship. In 2018, Trump hosted White and UFC champion Colby Covington at the White House during his first presidential term and later became a regular guest at UFC events as a sitting president. 
White also gave speeches in support of Trump at the Republican National Convention ahead of all three of his election cycles between 2016 and 2024.

description: There's no Shohei Ohtani- or Yoshinobu Yamamato-level player this winter, but there's still plenty of overseas ta
body:
There's no Shohei Ohtani- or Yoshinobu Yamamato-level player this winter, but there's still plenty of overseas talent available
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Major League Baseball's free agency period opened earlier this week and teams are now clear to pursue any roster upgrades they deem necessary. That includes players coming over from Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league, South Korea's Korea Baseball Organization, and Taiwan's Chinese Professional Baseball League. Those are high-level leagues that have sent many impact players MLB's way over the years. Look no farther than the Dodgers to see how important international talent can be to a club. The Dodgers employed four different former NPB and KBO players this past season, including two-way star Shohei Ohtani, ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and starter Roki Sasaki. Ohtani was signed as an MLB free agent, but the others went to the Dodgers through the posting system. Per the posting agreement with MLB, posted NPB and CPBL players get a 45-day window to negotiate and sign with an MLB team. KBO players get a 30-day window. Players who do not sign during that posting window return to their previous team in NPB, CPBL, or KBO. The MLB team that signs a posted player pays a fee to the player's former NPB, CPBL, or KBO team.Here is the posting fee structure: Contract valuePosting fee$25M or less 				 				 				20% of contract value 				 				 				$25M to $50M 				 				 				$5M plus 17.5% of contract value over $25M 				 				 				$50M or more 				 				 				$9.375M plus 15% of contract value over $50M 				 				 				For example, the White Sox paid Munetaka Murakami's former team, the Yakult Swallows, a $6.575 million posting fee on his $34 million contract last offseason. That's $5 million on the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the remaining $9 million, which is $1.575 million. The $5 million plus $1.575 million equals the $6.575 million posting fee paid to the Swallows.   Unlike last lockout, MLB will not be pausing the signing window during the expected lockout, according to The Athletic. In other words, if owners lock players out on Dec. 1 as expected, that date will essentially serve as the same deadline for already posted NPB players unless the lockout ends before their 45-day window expires.There are no superstar-caliber players like Ohtani or Yamamoto available in this winter's international free agent crop. There are, however, several interesting players who can improve an MLB roster in 2027. Here are the six best NPB, CPBL, and KBO players to know this offseason. 1. 3B Teruaki Sato Top 50 free agent ranking: No. 4Possible landing spots: Cardinals, Phillies, YankeesJapan's Triple Crown winner hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. He has a similar skill set to Murakami but is not exactly Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games in 2026 around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll. The Hanshin Tigers officially posted Sato on Nov. 1.2. RHP Kaima Taira Top 50 free agent ranking: 19Possible landing spots: Dodgers, Giants, PadresListed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Taira was officially posted on Nov. 1.3. RHP Hiroki Itoh Top 50 free agent ranking: No. 26Possible landing spots: Angels, Giants, PadresA down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters posted Itoh on Nov. 1. 4. 3B Si-Hwan Roh Top 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Marlins, Pirates, RedsRoh has an unusual agreement with the Hanwha Eagles. He signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and roughly $23 million), and as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him for MLB teams this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the Eagles to finish his career when his big-league stint is over. This past season, Roh, 26 in November, authored a .283/.360/.505 batting line with 29 home runs. He has real right-handed power and a good approach at the plate. There are concerns about his propensity to swing and miss as well as his arm at the hot corner. The Eagles formally posted Roh on Nov. 1.
5. RHP Kona Takahashi Top 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Diamondbacks, Rays, White SoxThe Seibu Lions posted Takahashi last offseason, but he was unable to find a contract to his liking, so he returned to Japan for another season and threw 148 innings with a 2.64 ERA. Takahashi, 30 in February, is an international free agent now, meaning he does not have to be posted and can instead negotiate at his own pace. More of a ground ball pitcher than a bat-misser, Takahashi sits in the 91-95 mph range with his fastball and has two good secondary pitches in his slider and splitter. He also throws a cutter and curveball. Takahashi is considered a potential innings guy for the back of an MLB rotation.6. RHP Jyun-Yue TsengTop 50 free agent ranking: UnrankedPossible landing spots: Athletics, MarinersTseng pitched for Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic in 2023 and 2026 and he has been one of the CPBL's top relievers the last few years. In 2026, he saved 25 games with a 1.80 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 52 ⅓ innings. Tseng's fastball typically sits in the mid-90s and has run as high as 100 mph in the past, though it has been a few years. His go-to secondary pitch is a breaking ball that needs improvement for Tseng to carve out an MLB career as more than a middle reliever.

        It's been 38 years since Lou Holtz got the win that defined his career at Notre Dame. On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program.No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title.The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely."They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings."
Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP.Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to knowDarian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader: Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen, its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy. Malachi Toney's absence: Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4.
CJ Carr's problem: Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College, SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule.Notre Dame's invincibility: Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005.Penalties and the red zone: Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own.
Where to watch Miami vs. Notre Dame live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ETLocation: Notre Dame Stadium -- South Bend, IndianaTV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction, picksNotre Dame opened as a 4.5-point favorite and is now laying 5.5, with the total at 57.5. History sides with the Irish. Now that Malachi Toney is out, siding with the Irish becomes an easy play. Notre Dame will play the nation's most efficient quarterback either way, but how different does he look without his top option? Meanwhile, Notre Dame's red-zone defense has struggled against far lesser offenses, so will Toney's absence actually matter? Miami is 5-3 against the spread this season. Notre Dame is 4-4. The Irish can win this game, but covering by five points will still be difficult. Pick: Miami +5.5

No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU liveDate: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, LouisianaTV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know  Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State, South Carolina and Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown, adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. 
LSU passing attack rounding into form: No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii, Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots: When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State.    Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks  While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Pick: Under 52.5

title: NFL fines Jaquan Brisker, two others for illegal Week 8 hits that placed opponents in concussion protocol - CBS Sports
description: Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
body:
Each of the players on the receiving end of those collisions will miss Week 9
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8, which was the second most in a single week this season. Among the most notable punishments were those handed down to Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn. Each fine was the result of a hit that led to the offensive player being placed in concussion protocol and ruled out for Week 9.Brisker owes the NFL $17,911 for a blow to the head/neck on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The play occurred less than a minute and a half into the Steelers' victory and drew a roughing the passer penalty, which Brisker voiced extreme displeasure with after the game."Babying the quarterback," Brisker said. "He's laying there crying, whatever he was doing. It is what it is. I assume I'm going to get fined because if you watch it, I'm hitting him with my chest and them I'm off to the side. But he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is."Watson briefly left the game, and Shedeur Sanders replaced him. The latter threw two passes before Watson returned to action and finished the game. Although Watson practiced in the days leading up to this Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints and cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday, the Browns announced they will turn to Sanders as their Week 9 starter.
Overshown's fine is for his use of his helmet on a hit against Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight. He must pay $9,528. The hit jarred the ball loose from Knight's hands, and the Cowboys recovered the fumble without a penalty. The NFL reviewed the play in the wake of the game, however, and issued the fine.
Knight will not play in the Cardinals' divisional clash with the Seattle Seahawks. He did not practice this week.
Chinn sealed a Raiders win last week with an interception in the end zone, but just one play prior, he made forcible contact with New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a catch along the sideline, which resulted in a fine. Chinn owes $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player. The two players' helmets collided on the play, and while Wilson stayed in the game for the Jets' final snap, he later entered concussion protocol.Wilson reported concussion symptoms the next day, and by midweek the Jets placed him in the protocol. They eventually ruled him out for this week's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs.
There have been 223 plays this season which resulted in a fine. That is 0.0113% of all plays through eight weeks. The 31 fines from Week 8 were second only to the 38 in Week 2.

title: Zuffa Boxing 12 results: Cheavon Clarke gets upset win, Da'Mazion Vanhouter shines - CBS Sports
description: Clarke continued to have Billam-Smith's number in the pros on Saturday night in London

Clarke continued to have Billam-Smith's number in the pros on Saturday night in London

        After twice scoring upset decisions over former cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith in their amateur days, former British Olympian Cheavon Clarke added an upset stoppage victory Saturday over his rival in the pro ranks at Zuffa Boxing 12.  Clarke (13-2, 10 KOs), a native of Jamaica who trains out of the U.K., took out the nearly 5-to-1 betting favorite in Billam-Smith (22-3, 14 KOs) during the main event of the Zuffa-promoted card inside Copper Box Arena in London. Nicknamed "C4," Clarke twice dropped Billam-Smith in the seventh round before referee Lee Every stopped the bout at 1:24 of the round while CBS was pinned against the ropes. Billam-Smith, a 36-year-old from the United Kingdom, lost a pair of 2016 amateur bouts to Clarke, including in the final of the British national championships and later that year in the English Title Series. "It has been 10 years, but I don't have no beef with Chris," Clarke said. "He has been the world champion, so give him his credit. I'm not going to be someone I'm not [and disrespect him]. Shout out to Chris."
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch Zuffa Boxing for no additional fee -- along with every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!After Billam-Smith lost his WBO cruiserweight title via decision to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024, he won his next two fights, including an all-action slugfest with Ryan Rozicki in June that marked his Zuffa debut as "CBS" scored a 7th-round TKO.  The fight against Clarke, 35, was physical from the jump, with both boxers looking to establish themselves on the inside, which led to a series of clinching throughout the first half of the scheduled 10-round bout.
Billam-Smith began to work the body aggressively before Clarke turned the momentum in his direction in Round 5 when he worked from long distance and hurt CBS with a clean right cross.  
"[Billam-Smith] is a strong guy," Clarke said. "Look, he's bigger than me. Most of these guys are bullying me, but I've never been bullied. My mom wouldn't have condoned it, so there you go."I don't need to prove anyone right other than myself. I believe in me and believe in my team," Clarke said. "I don't believe anybody trains as hard as me. They can try, but they don't." 
Clarke opened Round 7 by scoring a clean knockdown on another right hand. Billam-Smith regained his feet but went down a second time on another right hand. Even though "CBS" regained his feet, his legs began to wobble and Clarke let his hands go enough to force the stoppage. "I'm fine, it was a good shot, obviously," Billam-Smith said. "I made a mistake, but I felt like I was winning the fight, but fair play to Shep. We have had three fights and he has won them all, but I would love to run it back and get him eventually."Clarke won his third straight fight since dropping a pair of decisions to Leonardo Mosquea and Viddal Riley. In June, on the CBS-Rozicki undercard, Clarke stopped Jack Massey in a 7th-round TKO. 
Former middleweight titleholder Denzel Bentley wins Zuffa debut Bentley, who was stripped of his WBO middleweight title late last month after signing on for his Zuffa Boxing debut, held off a gritty effort by veteran Shane Mosley Jr. to claim a unanimous decision on scores of 96-93, 95-94 and 96-94 over a competitive 10 rounds. Mosley (23-6, 13 KOs), the 35-year-old son of Hall-of-Famer Shane Mosley Sr., got up from a crushing right hand that dropped him in Round 2 and survived a further barrage of punches to work his way back during the same round. "I cracked [Mosley's chin], but he got up," Bentley said. "I thought he was gone. I thought if I put a lot of shots on him, he wouldn't hold up, but he came back."
Bentley (23-3-1, 18 KOs), a 31-year-old who was fighting in his home city, held Mosley off down the stretch and, after the win, called for a shot at Carlos Adames, the WBC middleweight title who makes his Zuffa debut next week in Saudi Arabia, or a showdown against Conor Benn, who was seated ringside."I was fighting more than just Shane Mosley Jr. out here; I felt like I was fighting the whole of boxing for some of the decisions I had recently made," Bentley said. "It would've been even sweeter if the belt was on the line and I could've defended my title." Young heavyweight Da'Mazion Vanhouter continues red-hot start with knockoutAt just 21 and appearing on his fourth Zuffa card of 2026, Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) remained unbeaten with a first-round knockout of Ivan Balaz (9-2, 7 KOs). Vanhouter recorded a trio of knockdowns – all on body shots – before the fight was stopped at 2:04 by referee Kieran McCann. 
Vanhouter scored his eighth consecutive knockout since a 2024 split-decision win over Cristian Rodriguez and improved to 4-0 with four stoppages inside of three rounds since signing with Zuffa Boxing. 
After the fight, UFC president and CEO Dana White, who ringside in London, said he hoped to bring Vanhouter back for a fifth fight this year on Dec. 11 in Wales on the undercard of the long-awaited British heavyweight clash between former champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

title: Amid Oregon's shortcomings in 2026, Dan Lanning is turning in his best performance yet as Ducks coach - CBS Sports
description: Oregon might fall short of a national title, but navigating a QB crisis, firing an offensive coordinator and stun
body:
Oregon might fall short of a national title, but navigating a QB crisis, firing an offensive coordinator and stunning Ohio State represents the best coaching job of Lanning's career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A couple of months from now, Dan Lanning might look back at an Oregon season in which the Ducks fell short of all their primary goals. There's a strong chance they won't win the Big Ten, and there's a good chance they won't even reach the College Football Playoff, let alone win a national title.And as Lanning looks back, he may realize that 2026 was his greatest season as a head coach.Lanning's criticisms as a head coach have been consistent since he first stood on the sidelines at Oregon and watched his team get decimated by Georgia 49-3 to open the 2022 season. He's a great recruiter and motivator, but he's not a game-day coach. That's why his teams come up short so often in the biggest games when they can't just "out-talent" their opposition.But if those criticisms are true, explain how Oregon is 6-3 right now after beating Ohio State 41-28 in The Horseshoe on Saturday.
Oregon's season on the brinkEverything that could go wrong for Oregon in 2026 went wrong. It started the season looking like a team that had read all the press clippings about how great it would be. The Ducks seemed to lack a sense of urgency in a close win over Boise State to open the season, and they suffered a shocking upset loss a week later against Oklahoma State.The primary concern about Oregon heading into the year had to do with having two new coordinators on both sides of the ball. They were internal promotions, not big-name hires. The concerns seemed well-founded, with both the offense and defense struggling to start.Two weeks after the Oklahoma State loss, it looked like the season would truly spiral out of control. Dante Moore took a vicious hit while sliding and was knocked out of the game against USC. The Ducks rallied and won without him, but Moore hasn't played since and is out for the year. In his first start, Dylan Raiola and the offense turned the ball over seven times in a 17-15 home loss to UCLA. That loss led to Raiola, a high-priced transfer brought in to back up Moore and await his turn to start in 2027, being benched for Brock Thomas. Thomas struggled mightily a week later against Nebraska, and then it was Raiola coming in to lead a game-winning fourth-quarter drive.
Things seemed to have settled down. The Ducks were 4-2, but still had everything to play for. Then they went on the road to face an Illinois team forced to start a true freshman at QB due to its own QB injuries. And Illinois won. The Ducks suffered their third loss of the season before the end of October. The moment Lanning changed courseIt was a perilous situation. There have been plenty of examples of teams that came into a season with high expectations and effectively quit on the season once things went south. It's become more prevalent in the transfer portal era, since not everybody in the locker room has the same connection to a program that they may have had a decade ago.
But Lanning kept his team together despite all the evidence that they were toast. He made the difficult decision to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. It was an admission of a mistake, and one plenty of coaches have refused to make because pride wouldn't let them tell the world they messed up.The following week, they found themselves down 14 points to Northwestern. Another opportunity to lay down. Instead, the Ducks fought back to beat the Wildcats 34-26. On Saturday, Ohio State came out of the gates hot and stormed out to a 14-0 lead. Another opportunity for Oregon to quit, and another offer denied. It was 38-14 by the time Ohio State scored again. Ohio Stadium had begun to empty long before. 
Now, all of a sudden, Oregon sits at 6-3 with a shot. It might not be a great one, but it's there. The Ducks are through the most difficult stretch of their schedule and will finish with home games against Michigan and Washington, with a road trip to 2-6 Michigan State in between.The offense has looked much more comfortable since the OC change. The defense has had its act together for over a month at this point. I don't know if Oregon will win out, nor do I know if it'll reach the College Football Playoff. I suspect it won't. But I've been more impressed by Dan Lanning as a head coach for how he's handled things when damn near everything that could've gone wrong did. You learn a lot more from failure than success, and Lanning has learned a whole hell of a lot in 2026.
Maybe one day the lessons of this season will help Lanning and Oregon accomplish the goals they aren't likely to accomplish this time around.

title: Lane Kiffin falls flat against Alabama as massive LSU hype crashes into reality - CBS Sports
description: A $91 million contract and the sport's priciest roster haven't translated to the big stage as the Tigers drop to
body:
A $91 million contract and the sport's priciest roster haven't translated to the big stage as the Tigers drop to 0-3 against ranked teams after another humbling against Alabama
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Lane Kiffin got off the bus for the Tiger Walk before the Alabama game, he was flanked by Shaquille O'Neal and Angel Reese. Kevin Costner -- Kevin freaking Costner! -- walked behind him and shook his hand. No one has brought more attention and hype to a college football program this year than Kiffin. He signed a seven-year, $91 million contract, tied with two-time national champion Kirby Smart for the second-highest in college football. According to 247Sports, his roster is the most expensive in college football, approaching $50 million. And then, Alabama walked into the building. The Field of Dreams turned into a nightmare. No. 14 LSU collapsed under the weight of expectation against No. 5 Alabama, losing 31-13 in blowout fashion. After taking a 13-10 lead in the third quarter, the Tigers allowed 21 unanswered points for Kiffin's sixth straight loss against the Crimson Tide. 
With the loss, LSU sits at 6-3 and 0-3 against teams in the CFP Rankings. Their most impressive performance is arguably a one-point loss to No. 6 Kentucky on the road. While Kiffin has raised LSU's floor, putting unranked teams into the dirt, he has no-showed against real national competition. In every high-leverage moment, Alabama smoked LSU. The Tide held LSU to a field goal after first-and-goal. They forced a missed field goal, then set up a touchdown from great field position. LSU turned it over on downs three times, including twice in the fourth quarter, and turned the ball over twice. And what makes matters worse is that Kiffin's signature offense was completely outdueled by Alabama defensive coordinator Kane Wommack. Statistically, LSU managed to put up 457 yards, but the numbers go deeper. They finished in the 19th percentile for yards per play, 20th percentile for EPA per play and 1st percentile for Explosive Play Rate, according to Game on Paper. 
Essentially, LSU didn't do anything to truly force Alabama's defense to adjust. That's a hard pill to swallow when you've built your career on being an offensive savant. Kiffin had a great run at Ole Miss, elevating the program to new heights, especially by working with the Grove Collective to improve their NIL operation. With his roster left behind, Pete Golding led Ole Miss to the national semifinals last year. Kiffin has still never actually coached a postseason game, a streak that will likely continue this year. LSU still has two more shots against No. 7 Texas and No. 13 Tennessee for ranked wins, but the Tigers team that shows up against elite teams simply isn't good enough to win both games. If they split the result, LSU would finish 8-4 with a 1-4 record against CFP Top 25 opponents. 
After the season, most of the best players on the roster will be gone to the NFL. Kiffin will have to start all over again, building through the transfer portal. For the first time since 2016, the top two recruits in Louisiana are heading out of state. Adding insult to injury, No. 3 quarterback Elijah Haven -- a Baton Rouge native -- picked Kalen DeBoer and the Tide over Kiffin. Kiffin walked into Baton Rouge with an unbelievable amount of hype, landing Vanity Fair covers and dominating the interview circuit. When he got the job, Louisiana senator John Kenny joked, all of this nonsense is worth it -- but he better win. Well, Kiffin isn't winning. And after yet another embarrassing loss to Alabama, he could be heading for a painful offseason.

title: Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals, end 10-game unbeaten streak for Angel City - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals after extra time penalty in 1-0 win over Angel City FC
body:
Kansas City Current advance to NWSL semifinals after extra time penalty in 1-0 win over Angel City FC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two teams that tied for the most goals scored in the 2026 NWSL regular season played to a narrow scoreline over 120 minutes at CPKC Stadium on Saturday. Kansas City Current, last year's NWSL Shield winners, finally got a playoff win, taking the match 1-0 after extra time. Angel City, with a 10-game unbeaten streak now snapped, said farewell to the postseason.It was a result that may not tell the full story of the potential attacks on the pitch. Both teams scored 54 goals in the regular season, but the quarterfinal quickly turned into a defensive battle destined for a penalty shootout. Instead, the tense game tightened, went to extra time, and a penalty call changed the trajectory when Michelle Cooper converted the kick for the Current.One year after a playoff loss to Gotham ended their season at home, the exorcised some of their postseason demons, beating Angel City to extend their 16-match unbeaten run at CPKC Stadium and advance to the semifinals.Here's how the match unfolded:A defensive game in regulationMany were hoping for fireworks in the attacking third, but outside of a few looks, both sides got into dangerous spaces and produced only goalkeeping highlights. One of Kansas City's best chances of the opening half came inside of 20 minutes, as the trio of Haley Hopkins, Temwa Chawinga and Cooper combined for a header that went straight into the hands of goalkeeper Angelina Anderson.
Angel City showed off their impressive defensive shape, limiting the Current's press and slowing the tempo. Both teams at times even stayed more compact than usual, and Current goalkeeper Lorena was also forced to make a key save at the other end, shortly after Chawinga's attempt. 
"It was definitely a team effort. They played a lot of long balls, so winning the second ball was key for us," said Current center back Gabrielle Robinson, talking about the defensive shape."I think our sixes, our front line, was coming back and winning those second balls. But for us, is winning the first one, winning the second, and then turning around and going from there [were keys]. And I thought we were really good with that today."
Angel City's missed opportunityAngel City's midseason turnaround was a main storyline heading into the quarterfinals. The club appointed Leif Gunnar Smerud as interim head coach after parting ways with former manager Alexander Straus, and brought in Ally Sentnor in a summer trade with Kansas City Current.The return of defender Savy King from injury reset the backline, as she slotted in at right back and pushed Gisele Thompson to play as a wide midfielder for the remainder of the season. Team captain Sarah Gorden elevated her play alongside center back partner Emily Sams, and left back Evelyn Shores led the team with eight assists. Their 10-game unbeaten streak made them a team to watch in the playoffs, especially given the opponent.Angel City beat Kansas City Current earlier in the regular season, then drew 1-1 at CPKC Stadium in August. The group's ability to keep the Current off the scoreboard in regulation was valiant, with Anderson making a massive save in stoppage time of regulation. 
"Listen, I don't always take the opportunity to make an opening statement here, but I did this time because I want to congratulate Angel City on a great season. And it's a shame that one of us on the day was not going to move on. But they're a tough team. They were hard to play against for sure. They gave us everything, and I think we gave them everything," Current manager Chris Armas said in postgame comments."It was a good game, and you can see what it meant to that team. They left everything on the field. So to Leif, the head coach over there, I think he did a great job this season taking over, and they have a lot to be proud of. They're a great team, and just wanted to acknowledge that."Kansas City's playoff momentExtra time proved to be Kansas City's time, even with what some will deem a peculiar penalty call. Plenty of set pieces were awarded during the quarterfinal -- eight corners for Kansas City and 11 for Angel City -- with Angel City midfielder Ary Borges and Current center back Kayla Sharples often jockeying for position in the box.
On a set piece delivery from Izzy Rodriguez, the center official called a penalty for a pushing foul by Angel City keeper Anderson, and after a quick confirmation, the rare call stood and Cooper converted for the Current. 
Cooper's big moment was almost like a passing of the torch, as team captain Lo'eau LaBonta is typically the lead penalty taker. Armas later confirmed in postgame that had the game gone into penalties, the captain would've taken one, but in extra time the moment was Cooper's."[LaBonta] has scored so many in her career. Understands what it feels like at the spot. And even in those moments when she grabs the ball, you know she's maybe protecting Coop in that moment to then hand it off to her. I don't even know if they've had a discussion, but if they did and it went back to Lo, I would trust that she could take it. But this was something ahead of time. We knew Coop would take it, and she buried it," Armas said.
Cooper's big playoff moment was long overdue. The forward missed last year's disappointing quarterfinal exit because of a lingering foot injury. Now, she's back, with the game-winning goal under her belt."I always want to contribute and help my teammates when I can. So, it was, like, really shitty last year when I got injured, literally right before. But it's part of the game, and I think I supported them the best I could last year. To be able to actually impact the game in a way of scoring a goal in the PK, and converting, it's felt really good. But I think, I can't celebrate yet. We still have two more games to go, one game guaranteed next weekend, and that's honestly the biggest focus for me," Cooper said."I think we can come up with a lot of like reasons and excuses. I could say for last year and why it didn't really fall our way, but I think this team this year has taken things personal and never-say-die, and that's kind of the mentality that we've been going with, and we just want to keep it rolling. So that's been the biggest change for us, I think, this year," she said.
What's nextKansas City Current will face the winner of the Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign quarterfinal on Sunday. The NWSL semifinals will take place on Nov. 14 and 15.

An injured reserve stint delayed the first look at Garrett and Donald in the same lineup, but now they could dominate opposing offenses

    3:38 pm ET

        When Los Angeles Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returns from injured reserve this week for his first game action since the season opener, he will line up next to defensive lineman Aaron Donald for the first time. That duo is projected to be one of the NFL's most unstoppable tandems at any position since Donald announced that he would come out of retirement for the 2026 season, and now the league will find out just how formidable it really is.The timing of Garrett's IR stint and Donald's season debut clashed, forcing them to wait until November to suit up together. Garrett played just one game before he underwent knee surgery, and Donald entered the lineup in Week 2.Garrett said it will be surreal to share the field with a fellow Defensive Player of the Year award winner."Going into this season, I never thought I'd have the chance," Garrett said ahead of Sunday's road game against the Washington Commanders. "As y'all know, he kept us in suspense for quite a while. It was very exciting to hear about that. Looking forward to the opportunity to get on the field and actually play some real snaps with him."
Garrett's arrival in Los Angeles by way of a blockbuster trade in June was a catalyst for Donald's unretirement, so it is only right that two of the most disruptive players in football history finally get the opportunity to play alongside each other. Donald has been more effective in run defense than pass rushing this season, so with Garrett (the single-season sack record holder) rejoining the fold, their skill sets should complement each other tremendously.Both superstar defenders have commanded double teams at extreme rates throughout their careers, but opposing offensive lines might have to stay more honest with their assignments so as to prevent the other player from capitalizing on the diverted attention."I think offenses really have to pick their poison," Garrett said. "Who's going to be freed up this play? Either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-ones. We'll have some fun."
There is no better time than the present for Garrett to return to full strength and for this duo to join forces. The Rams are in the midst of a potential midseason turnaround after opening the year with a surprising yet immensely disappointing 2-4 record, and they need to keep the momentum rolling to fulfill their Super Bowl expectations.How will Myles Garrett fare in his return?At the time, it was a surprise to see Garrett held entirely in check in the season-opening blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. When the news of his knee ailment came to light, though, it explained why he was held without a single tackle in the contest. Garrett said that the knee acted up on him throughout the game and limited him from making his typical impact as a first-team All-Pro-caliber force off the edge.Now that he is healthy, the question is just how great of an impact Garrett will make for the elite Rams defense. Every year since his rookie season, the former No. 1 overall pick has logged double-digit sacks. Last season, he broke the NFL single-season record with 23. He is also a stalwart in run defense and led the league in tackles of loss each of the last two years.
There was one sign in Week 1 that suggested Garrett will deliver his usual impact and perhaps even take another step forward in his first year with the Rams. He logged five quarterback pressures on Brock Purdy in that loss to the 49ers, good for an 18.5% pressure rate on his 39 defensive snaps. That would be the third-best mark of his career if it sustained over a full season.

        The sellout crowd inside Williams-Brice Stadium held its collective breath Saturday in the second quarter after South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was sandwiched between defenders on a sack against Texas A&M and had to leave the game with an injury.Sellers was slow to get up after losing a fumble on the play at the Aggies' 18-yard line, grabbing his left ankle before hobbling off to the sideline with the help of team trainers. Sellers re-entered the contest to open the third quarter during South Carolina's first possession and showed no ill effects of the first-half injury. Sellers exited the injury tent on his own power, slowly walking toward the locker room with just over four minutes to play before intermission."We're concerned," South Carolina coach Shane Beamer told the ESPN broadcast at halftime. "He's got an ankle, and he's getting an X-ray on it. I don't have anything else."
The Gamecocks (5-3), slotted No. 21 in the first College Football Playoff rankings on the heels of three straight wins, need their best player available the rest of the way to remain in the postseason conversation.Sellers was 10-of-15 for 151 yards and a touchdown in Saturday's game before leaving. Sellers has accounted for 13 touchdowns during South Carolina's current win streak and was named the AP's National Player of the Week last time out after registering 397 yards of total offense and five touchdowns at Oklahoma.
Sellers threw an 84-yard touchdown pass to DJ Black and a 79-yard toss to Mazeo Bennett to highlight his performance. Both plays were made off schedule with Sellers outside of the pocket."Those are great plays. I mean, you worry about those plays from a protection standpoint, so you see him get the ball off," Beamer said after that win. "And I'm proud of our guys, too. When the quarterback scrambles, it's not like everybody just runs around blindly. Like, we have a plan of what needs to happen when the quarterback scrambles, and we worked a lot of that on the bye week. "We talked about it this morning in our staff meeting: that, make sure we're big on scrambles because they're really, really good on defense, and they're probably going to get some pressure on our quarterback, and we've got a chance to hit some big plays in the passing game if we do. So, great to see those guys execute the scramble drills the right way.
